anchor.quote: Treaties are made under international law. Follow the correct style to help people to access titles, series information and detailed citations.

not_rules.note: Introductory advice to follow style.

anchor.quote: Treaty citations need the correct title and series information

not_rules.note: Section heading grouping rules on title and series information.

anchor.quote: A treaty is an international agreement that is binding under international law. The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade explains the different types of treaties and how they are made in the Treaty making process.

not_rules.note: Contextual description of what treaties are.

anchor.quote: Sometimes a Commonwealth Act of parliament is required to give effect to a treaty – for example, the Antarctic Treaty Act 1960.

not_rules.note: Contextual description regarding implementation.

anchor.quote: Treaties also include conventions, international agreements, covenants, an exchange of letters, international instruments, charters or protocols.

not_rules.note: Defines what falls under treaties.

anchor.quote: Treaties appear in various official series published by countries and international organisations.

not_rules.note: Information on where treaties are published.

anchor.quote: Australian treaties are published in the Australian Treaty Series (ATS). Other series include the United Nations Treaty Series (UNTS), the United States Treaties and Other International Agreements (UST) and the United Kingdom Treaty Series (UKTS).

not_rules.note: Examples of official series.

anchor.quote: To search for the titles, short titles and series information for treaties that Australia has signed or taken other action on, use the Australian Treaties Database. You can also use AustLII’s Australian Treaties Library.

not_rules.note: Advice on where to search for information.

anchor.quote: For other series, use the WorldLII Treaties and International Agreements database catalogue. Alternatively, go directly to the relevant databases. These include the United Nations Treaty Collection, UK Treaties Online and, for the US, Treaties and Other International Acts Series.

not_rules.note: Advice on resources and databases to use.

anchor.quote: In general publications, citing the title of the treaty is usually enough.

rules.quote: Write titles of treaties in roman type with title case (maximal capitalisation).
rules.violation_condition: a treaty title written in italics, bold, or in sentence case
rules.why: Restatement of the heading; specifies exact casing and typeface formatting for treaty titles.

examples.note: Shows the introduction of the short title in parentheses.

examples.note: Shows the introduction of the short title and its subsequent use.

parts.quote: Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and their Disposal (Basel Convention). Australian signed the Basel Convention in 1992.

rules.quote: Follow the full title with the short title in parentheses and use the short title after that.
rules.violation_condition: a treaty's short title introduced without first providing the full title, or the full title used again after the short title has been introduced
rules.why: A distinct rule regarding abbreviation introduction and usage for treaties.

covers.quote: If you include it, write it into the sentence or add it in parentheses after the short title.

examples.note: Shows the year correctly added in parentheses, not as part of the title.

rules.quote: The year the treaty is made does not form part of the title.
rules.violation_condition: a treaty title that includes the year it was made as part of the title itself
rules.why: The second sentence explains how to comply with the prohibition stated in the first, so they form one rule.

rules.violation_condition: a detailed treaty citation that does not include the required elements in the prescribed order (title, place and date, year entered into force, series and volume, page)
rules.why: Groups the citation format list items under their lead-in sentence to form a single testable format.

examples.note: Shows spaces but no punctuation between elements.

rules.quote: Don’t use any punctuation between the elements.
rules.violation_condition: a detailed treaty citation containing punctuation marks (such as commas or periods) separating the main citation elements
rules.why: Separate rule because this targets incorrect punctuation specifically, distinct from missing elements or bad order.

examples.note: Demonstrates using the long title in a reference list, despite using a short title in notes.

parts.quote: The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) entered into force on 23 March 1976.1 [In-text reference]
1 ICCPR (New York, 16 December 1966) [1980] ATS 23. [Short title in the note that gives the citation]
International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (New York, 16 December 1966) [1980] ATS 23. [Long title in reference list entry]

rules.quote: Always use the long title in a reference list.
rules.violation_condition: a treaty citation in a reference list that uses the short title instead of the long title
rules.why: Specific requirement for reference list entries regarding treaties.
